rationale: a and b tied (4.44). b supplies the spine and the clinical hook (24-year-old with migrating pain), the look-alikes by group (children, women, adults) on the O8 node reached on every path, and the cold which-is-not close with no hint. From a: a sure_note on every wrong tap, the Rovsing direction probe with its dominated option rewritten to carry a pressure word, and the contrast explainer. Judge fixes: hints no longer name the two 2-point items; first miss gives a nudge only (Try again / Show me why), the answer comes on the second miss or via Show me why; every probe has a reordered re-ask so key positions vary; options length-matched; 'Wrong:' openers and raw claim IDs removed from learner text; '@next' kept on the cl terminals. TR3 is probed three ways (a left-press option in the psoas case, the direction probe, and a Rovsing distractor in the obturator naming probe).
lesson: When two variants tie, take the one with the real clinical hook and cold close as the spine and graft the other's per-option hypercorrection notes and direction probe; give look-alike traps (signs sharing a limb) a probe in more than one form, and never let a hint name the key.
